R becomes especially powerful when code, statistical reasoning and communication live in one workflow.

```text
Import → Tidy → Transform → Visualize → Model → Communicate
```

::: {.callout-tip}
## Key ideas
`tidy data` `dplyr` `tidyr` `ggplot2` `readr`
`lm` `glm` `tidymodels` `Quarto` `reproducibility`
:::

## Core learning path

**R for Data Science (2e):**  
https://r4ds.hadley.nz/

It teaches the practical cycle of importing, transforming, visualizing and communicating data.

**ggplot2 book:**  
https://ggplot2-book.org/

**Tidy Modeling with R:**  
https://www.tmwr.org/

**tidymodels:**  
https://www.tidymodels.org/

**Quarto:**  
https://quarto.org/docs/get-started/

## One beautiful idea: formulas

```r
model <- lm(
  price ~ size + bedrooms + age,
  data = homes
)

summary(model)
```

R's formula interface connects programming directly to statistical model specification.

## Practice projects

Do not practice R only through isolated syntax exercises. Pick a dataset and repeatedly perform:

```text
question
 → clean
 → visualize
 → summarize
 → model
 → diagnose
 → communicate
```

The free R for Data Science book deliberately emphasizes this end-to-end workflow.

::: {.callout-tip}
## Where R shines
R is particularly strong when statistical analysis, visualization and reproducible scientific communication are central to the work.
:::
